Now That's What I Call An Era Such A Good Feeling 1988 >> 1995" is a compilation album released on September 26, 2025, by Sony Music and EMI as part of the Now Eras series. It focuses on the transformative period between 1988 and 1995 when electronic dance music, funk/soul, and pop converged to shape mainstream music and club culture. The album features 46 tracks on a 3LP colored vinyl edition, showcasing seminal dance and house anthems such as Brothers in Rhythm's "Such a Good Feeling," Black Box's "Ride on Time," and Deee-Lite's "Groove Is in the Heart," reflecting the vibrant club scene and evolving electronic sounds of the late 80s and early 90s.

Musically, the album captures the energy of house, rave, and club music that defined the era, blending electronic beats with soulful vocals and pop sensibilities. It serves as a historical snapshot within the Now That's What I Call Music franchise, which has expanded beyond current hits to curate era-defining collections. Critically, the compilation has been noted for its comprehensive track selection that highlights the period's dance culture impact on the UK and global charts. Commercially, it appeals to both nostalgic listeners and new audiences interested in the roots of modern electronic and dance music, supported by deluxe formats including a 4CD edition with 82 tracks and a hardcover book.
